profile.title: General product passport
profile.description: A voluntary profile. An obligation of "must" here means the record would not be a passport without the value, not that any law asks for it.
profile.regulatoryLine: No rule covers these products, and none is claimed. The record follows the same shape as the regulated profiles so a maker who later falls in scope is already close to it.

statements.text: No instrument requires a passport for these products, and none is cited as if one did; every field states that in its legal basis.

stamps.description: The sample marker a demonstration record carries first; never product data.
The profile identifier the payload declares.
The profile version the payload declares; a reader decodes under it and never under a newer one.
An optional physical-object DID carried in the public payload; carrying it does not implement physical binding.
The data-carrier identifier (chip UID) the lookup service indexes beside the passport identifier.

fields.label: Product name
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A record with no name is not a passport.
fields.note: What the maker calls it. Nothing else identifies an object to the person holding it.

fields.label: Kind of object
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It decides which of the fields below make sense.
fields.note: Open by definition: the whole point of this profile is that the list is not knowable.

fields.label: Maker
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. On a handbuilt object the maker is the claim.
fields.note: A workshop, a studio or a company; a name and nothing to constrain it to.

fields.label: How to reach the maker
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A guarantee nobody can claim against is decoration.
fields.note: An email, an address or a page. Constraining it to one shape would exclude the others.

fields.label: Model or reference
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is how a maker finds the drawings again.

fields.label: Serial number
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the commonest way an object proves it is the one.

fields.label: Where it was made
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Place is half of provenance.

fields.label: Made
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Age is what a durable object is judged on.

fields.label: Dimensions
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is what a second buyer asks first.
fields.note: A frame size, a case diameter, a seat height. No two categories measure alike.

fields.label: Weight
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.

fields.label: Edition
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. On a limited run it is most of the value.
fields.note: Numbered, limited, one of one, or a named run. Every workshop counts differently.

fields.label: Made by
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the difference between made and manufactured.
fields.note: The person, where a person can be named. A workshop is a company; a maker is not.

fields.label: How to tell it is the real one
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the question a passport exists to answer.
fields.note: Open: trades authenticate in ways this list will not have thought of.

fields.label: Certificate
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. The paper certificate, kept where it cannot be lost.

fields.label: Made for
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Published only where the first owner wanted it published.
fields.note: Who it was built for, where the first owner is part of the story.

fields.label: Materials
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the first thing a repairer needs and the last thing a recycler needs.

fields.label: How it was made
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is most of what a buyer is paying for.
fields.note: Open: crafts describe their own methods, and a closed list would flatten them.

fields.label: Finish
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: Lacquer, patina, plating, oil. The thing a restorer must not strip by mistake.

fields.label: Anything else worth recording
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is what keeps a declared profile usable for objects nobody has thought of.
fields.note: The declared fields cannot anticipate every craft, so one field stays open. It is a named field with a place in the record, not a freeform profile.

fields.label: Recycled content
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Declared where a maker can substantiate it.

fields.label: Substances to handle with care
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this here, though REACH Art. 33 may require it of the article itself.
fields.note: Lead solder, shellac, cadmium in old plating. Prose, because the reader is a person.

fields.label: How to look after it
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the single field most likely to extend the object’s life.
fields.note: The advice a maker gives when they hand it over, which no symbol set carries.

fields.label: Service interval
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: Every five years, every 5,000 km, after every season. No one unit fits.

fields.label: Expected lifetime
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A claim made here is one the maker can be held to.

fields.label: Guarantee
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires the figure, though a stated commercial guarantee binds the maker.

fields.label: Guarantee terms
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A term with no conditions attached is not a guarantee.

fields.label: What can be repaired
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: Which parts come off, and what needs the workshop. A score would say less.

fields.label: Spare parts
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is what decides whether the object outlives its owner.
fields.note: Which parts, and for how long. A yes/no would hide the part that matters.

fields.label: Repair notes
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.

fields.label: Where to get it repaired
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.

fields.label: Workshop notes
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Restricted because it is useless to a consumer and valuable to a repairer.
fields.note: Torque figures, thread sizes, the fixture that releases the part. Written for a trade, not a buyer.

fields.label: Where to return it
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A maker who takes it back says so here.
fields.note: A place and a method, in the words the person returning it will use.

fields.label: What can be recovered
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: What a recycler can actually do with it, which no percentage conveys.

fields.label: What comes apart
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: Which components separate, and how. The sentence a dismantler needs.

fields.label: Supply chain
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Declared by makers who treat their suppliers as a credential.

fields.label: Independent certification
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this.
fields.note: Open, and with no list at all: the schemes that matter differ completely between a violin and a bicycle, so nothing here could be exhaustive.

fields.label: Provenance
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is the owner tier the selective-disclosure demo turns on.
fields.note: The story of this particular object, which is prose by definition.

fields.label: Purchased
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. It is what makes the record theirs.
fields.note: Where and when, as the owner would write it.

fields.label: Fitting and setup
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. A fitted object is a different object to its owner.
fields.note: Saddle height, string gauge, engraving. Written by whoever set it up.

fields.label: Valuation reference
fields.legalBasis: Nothing requires this. Owner tier only, and no figure ever reaches the public payload.
fields.note: An insurer’s reference or an appraisal note. Never a price on the public record.

eventMappings.requires: manufacturing or commissioning evidence naming the facility, time and responsible party; the native ACTIVATE alone records only that a passport was opened

eventMappings.externalEvent: physical move or change of custody
eventMappings.requires: actual source and destination movement or custody evidence; a change of token control is not a shipment

eventMappings.externalEvent: physical move or change of custody
eventMappings.requires: actual source and destination movement or custody evidence
custody evidence beyond the token transfer; the transfer of token control alone establishes neither physical movement nor legal title
repair evidence naming what was done, by whom and when
nothing physical: an EDIT is a native metadata operation and maps to a record revision, not a physical transformation

eventMappings.externalEvent: disposition, or a process creating new products or materials
eventMappings.requires: recycling evidence distinguishing disposition of this item from a process whose outputs carry new identities

sourceRefs.name: Nothing. No instrument requires a passport for these products, and none is cited as if one did; every field states that in its legalRef.
sourceRefs.use: The honest statement of legal basis.

sourceRefs.name: The shape follows the regulated profiles so a maker who later falls in scope is already close to it.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
sourceRefs.use: Every value typed country. Officially assigned codes only; user-assigned and exceptionally-reserved codes are excluded so a passport cannot name a place no register resolves.

identity.passportIdentifier: A GS1 Digital Link URI carrying the GTIN under application identifier 01 and the serial under 21 (spec/record-model.md section 3); the enduring identifier never changes across the chain.

vectors.description: The bottle for a public audience: model and item values each name their source, the closure and label relationships are recorded without being entered, the return scheme and the producer-responsibility registration are carried as documents, and the content the bottle is part of is not read.
